seoTitle: Bedtime Calculator - When Should I Go To Sleep?
metaDescription: Calculate the exact time you should go to bed based on your wake-up time. Use 90-minute sleep cycles to wake up feeling completely refreshed.
intro: Do you have an early start tomorrow and need to know exactly when you should go to sleep tonight? Guessing your bedtime often leads to tossing and turning, or worse, waking up mid-dream feeling completely drained. Our free online Bedtime Calculator is designed to solve this exact problem. By entering the time your alarm is set to ring, the calculator works backward through standard human sleep cycles to give you the precise times you should turn off the lights. Aligning your bedtime with your natural 90-minute sleep rhythms ensures you wake up at the end of a cycle, making it vastly easier to get out of bed and start your day with high energy.
whatIs: The Bedtime Calculator is a reverse-engineering tool for your sleep schedule. Human sleep is not uniform; it consists of 90-minute cycles that oscillate between light sleep, deep restorative sleep, and REM (dreaming) sleep. Waking up during deep sleep causes severe grogginess (sleep inertia), while waking up at the end of a cycle feels natural and refreshing. This tool takes your mandatory wake-up time and subtracts sleep cycles to find the exact moments you should try to fall asleep. It is an essential utility for anyone with a strict morning schedule, shift workers adjusting to new hours, or anyone looking to improve their daily energy levels through better sleep hygiene.
howToUse: Select the time you need to wake up using the time picker.
Review the list of suggested bedtimes.
Try to be in bed by one of the 'Optimal' times to get 5 or 6 full sleep cycles.
howItWorks: When you input your required morning wake-up time, the calculator's algorithm performs a series of backward deductions. It first subtracts blocks of 90 minutes (representing one full sleep cycle). For a healthy adult, it calculates options for 6 cycles (9 hours), 5 cycles (7.5 hours), and 4 cycles (6 hours). Once it establishes these target sleep times, it subtracts an additional 15 minutes from each option. This 15-minute buffer accounts for 'sleep latency'—the time it takes the average person to actually fall asleep after getting into bed and closing their eyes. The resulting times displayed are the exact moments you should get into bed.
workedExample: Suppose you are starting a new job tomorrow and your alarm is set for 6:00 AM. You want to be well-rested, so you enter '6:00 AM' into the calculator. The tool works backward in 90-minute intervals. For an optimal 5 sleep cycles (7.5 hours of actual sleep), it lands on 10:30 PM. It then subtracts the 15-minute sleep latency buffer, resulting in a recommended bedtime of 10:15 PM. If you want maximum rest (6 cycles, or 9 hours), it suggests getting into bed at 8:45 PM. If you are running late and can only manage 4 cycles (6 hours), the tool advises you to be in bed by 11:45 PM.
resultInterpretation: The output provides a clear list of recommended bedtimes, usually highlighting the options for 5 or 6 cycles as the healthiest choices for most adults. The times shown represent when you should be physically in bed, with the lights off, actively trying to sleep. The 15 minutes required to fall asleep is already factored into these times. If you choose the 10:15 PM option from the example, and it takes you 15 minutes to fall asleep, you will enter your first sleep cycle at exactly 10:30 PM, complete five full cycles, and naturally transition to light sleep exactly at 6:00 AM when your alarm rings.
useCases: Early Flights: Knowing exactly when to sleep to catch a 5:00 AM flight without feeling like a zombie.
School/Work Routine: Establishing a healthy nightly routine to wake up for work or school easily.
Fixing Sleep Debt: Finding out the earliest optimal bedtime to catch up on lost sleep.
tipsAndLimitations: The 15-minute fall-asleep time is an average. Adjust your actual in-bed time if you know you fall asleep instantly or take an hour.
Avoid screens 30 minutes before your chosen bedtime to help you fall asleep on time.

faq.question: Is it better to sleep 6 hours or 7 hours?
faq.answer: Scientifically, sleeping 6 hours (exactly 4 cycles) or 7.5 hours (exactly 5 cycles) is usually better than 7 hours, because 7 hours wakes you up in the middle of a deep sleep cycle.

faq.question: How long is a sleep cycle?
faq.answer: The average human sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes, progressing from light sleep to deep sleep and REM sleep.

disclaimer: This tool relies on average human sleep cycles of 90 minutes. Consult a doctor for chronic sleep issues.
